THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
S G PANDIT J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Since these appeals are listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, they are taken up for final disposal.

2. The claimants-injured are before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation, not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded under judgment and award dated 10.07.2019 passed in MVC Nos.532/2016 and 533/2016 on the file of learned Prl. Senior Civil Judge & Member,
MACT, Jamkhandi1.
3.

Brief facts of the case leading to filing of these appeals are that, on 16.10.2014, both the claimants-injured were proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-10- BB-2968 from Sonyal Village.

When they reached near Kumbar 'Tribunal' for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:7930-DB Vasathi, near Tikota, at that time, Tata Maxi cab bearing registration No.KA-28/7877 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle, causing injuries to both the claimants.
It is stated that the claimant in MVC No.532/2016 was aged about 26 years at the time of accident and was doing agricultural work, earning Rs.12,000/- per month.

It is further stated that the claimant in Gajanan @ Gajanand S/O Dharageppa ... vs Chandrashekhar S/O Malleshappa ... on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141131991/
2 MVC No.533/2016 was aged about 29 years at the time of the accident and was a driver of tractor,
earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
4.

entities.text: Gajanan @ Gajanand S/O Dharageppa ... vs Chandrashekhar S/O Malleshappa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Both the claimants examined themselves as PW1 and PW3 and examined the doctor as PW2,
apart from marking the documents as Ex.P1 to P23.
The respondent No.2-insurer examined its Manager as RW1 and RTO of Vijayapur as RW2 apart from marking the documents as Ex.R1 to R5.

The Tribunal considering the material on record awarded total compensation of Rs.23,99,944/- in MVC No.533/2016 and Rs.2,46,059/- in MVC No.532/2016 with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petitions till realization.

Heard the learned counsel Sri. Siddappa Sajjan for the appellants/injured, learned counsel Sri.
N.R.Kuppelur for the respondent/insurance company and perused the appeal papers including original records.

6. Learned counsel Sri.Siddappa Sajjan for the appellants/injured would submit that the notional income of the injured-Gajanana assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.8,000/- per month is on the lower side, inasmuch as he was doing agricultural work and earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
He further submits that the award of compensation by the Tribunal under other heads is on the lower side and seeks to enhance the same.

7. Learned counsel Sri. Siddappa Sajjan further submits that the income of the injured-Mahadeva assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.10,000/- is on the lower side, since he was a driver of tractor, earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
It is submitted that to substantiate the said contention, the claimant has produced Ex.P23-Driving License.

He further submits that disability assessed by the Tribunal at 75% is on lesser side, since PW2-doctor has deposed that the claimant has suffered NC:
2024:KHC-D:7930-DB functional disability to an extent of 90% in respect of whole body.
He would further submit that the claimant is entitled for addition of 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects.
It is his submission that the award of compensation by the Tribunal on the other heads is also on the lower side and seeks to enhance the same.
Thus, he prays for allowing the appeals filed by the appellants/injured.

8. Per contra, learned counsel Sri. N.R.Kuppelur for the respondent/Insurance company supporting the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal contends that the Tribunal considering oral and documentary evidence on record awarded just and reasonable compensation under various heads in respect of both the claimants, which does not call for interference at the hands of this Court.

Thus,
he prays for dismissal of the appeals.

9. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers including original records, the following points would arise for consideration in these appeals:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7930-DB Gajanan @ Gajanand S/O Dharageppa ... vs Chandrashekhar S/O Malleshappa ... on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141131991/
3 a)Whether the disability assessed by the Tribunal at 75% to the whole body is proper and correct?
b)
Whether the notional income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.10,000/- per month is just and proper?
c) Whether the claimant would be entitled for addition of 40% towards future prospects?
Points No.(a) and (c) are answered in the "affirmative" and point No.(b) is answered in the "negative" for the following reasons.
Whether the claimant would be entitled for enhanced compensation?

Answer to the above point would be in the affirmative for the following reasons:
10. Indisputably, the accident occurred on 16.10.2014 involving motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-10-BB-2968 and Tata Maxi Cab bearing registration No.KA-28/7877, resulting in injuries to both the appellants/injured.
Both the claimants-injured are before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation.
Admittedly, the insurance NC: 2024:KHC-D:7930-DB company has not filed any appeal and it has satisfied the award of the Tribunal.
11. In MFA No.103625/2019 (MVC No.533/2016), the claimant-Mahadeva examined as PW1 and doctor examined as PW2.

In terms of Ex.P5-Wound Certificate, the claimant has suffered following injuries:
a) Two lacerated wounds present on right side of the face measuring 6 x 1cm x muscle deep and 4 x 1 x muscle deep along with surrounding abrasions and bleeding;
b) Right thigh deformity present;
c) Fracture with protrusion of femoral head and fracture of right femur with displacement and overlapping.
d) Multiple scratch abrasions present on outer aspect of the right leg.
e) Split laceration present on medial border of right foot measuring 8 x 3cm x bone deep with lower end of tibia protruding with bleeding.
12.
The claimant was an inpatient for about 52 days.

PW2-doctor has deposed in his chief-examination that considering all clinical and radiological findings, he was of the opinion that the claimant has got permanent physical disability to an extent of 75% to the whole body in view of hemiplegics, right side and 50% to the right hip, 30% to right knee and 50% NC:
2024:KHC-D:7930-DB to right ankle and 90% to whole body.

The doctor has opined that the Gajanan @ Gajanand S/O Dharageppa ... vs Chandrashekhar S/O Malleshappa ... on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141131991/
4 claimant has suffered 90% disability to the whole body.

entities.text: Gajanan @ Gajanand S/O Dharageppa ... vs Chandrashekhar S/O Malleshappa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW2-doctor in his cross-examination has stated that bones are united and though bones are united, it would be difficult for the injured to move around.

Admittedly, the claimant was working as driver and to prove his avocation,
Ex.P23-Driving License is placed on record.
The Tribunal, taking note of injuries sustained by the claimant, evidence of PW2-doctor both oral and documentary, has rightly assessed whole body disability at 75%, which needs no interference.
13. It is stated that the claimant was working as driver of Tractor and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
To prove his avocation, the claimant has placed on record Ex.P23-Driving License, which would indicate that he had license to drive LMV as well as Tractor-trailer.

In the circumstances,
notional income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.10,000/- per month is on the lower side.

The driver,
who possesses driving license to drive LMV as well as Tractor-trailer would have earned more than Rs.10,000/- per month.
Hence, we deem it appropriate to re-assess the notional income of the injured at Rs.12,000/- per month.

There is no dispute with regard to age of the claimant NC:
2024:KHC-D:7930-DB as 29 years and appropriate multiplier of 17.

Due to the accidental injuries,
the claimant is not in a position to drive any kind of vehicle.

Therefore, taking note of the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant as well as his avocation as driver and disability assessed at 75% to whole body, we are of the opinion that the claimant would be entitled for addition of 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects.

Thus, the claimant would be entitled to modified compensation under the head of loss of future earning due to disability as under:
Rs.12,000 + 40% x 12 x 17 x 75% = Rs.25,70,400/-
14.

Taking note of the injuries suffered by the claimant, evidence of PW2-doctor and duration of treatment taken by him, we deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering as against Rs.25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has not granted any compensation on the head of loss of amenities.
Looking into the injuries sustained and the disability suffered by the claimant, we deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards loss of amenities.
The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.8,14,944/- towards medical expenses, as per medical bills produced by the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7930-DB claimant, which is undisturbed.

Thus, the claimant is entitled to modified compensation on the following heads:

. No .

Particulars Amount 1. Loss of earning capacity Rs.25,70,400/-
2. Pain and suffering Rs. 50,000/-
3. Loss of amenities Rs. 75,000/-
4. Medical expenses Rs. 8,14,944/-
5. Food, Nourishment, attendant Rs. 30,000/-
 charges, conveyance etc.
 Total Rs.35,40,344/-

5 15.
Thus, the claimant-Mahadeva is entitled to total compensation of Rs.35,40,344/- as against Rs.23,99,944/- awarded by the Tribunal.
16. In MFA No.103626/2019 (MVC No.532/2016), the claimant-Gajanan examined as PW3 and doctor examined as CW1-Dr. Basavaraj.

In terms of Ex.C2-Disability Certificate, the claimant has suffered following injuries:
a) Displaced fracture of bilateral body and right ramous of mandible.
b) Split laceration present on middle of the right chin measuring 3 x 1 x bone deep with bleeding.
c) Multiple scratch abrasions present on other aspect of right leg and right foot with mild bleeding.
17. CW1-doctor has opined that the claimant has got permanent physical disability to an extent of 35% of - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7930-DB Dentofacial complex.

Taking note of evidence of CW1 coupled with Ex.C2-Disabilty Certificate, the Tribunal assessed the disability of the injured at 11.5% to the whole body, which in our view is just and proper, does not call for interference.
It is stated that the claimant-Gajanan is an agriculturist, earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
The Tribunal assessed monthly income of the injured at Rs.8,000/- per month, which is also just and proper and same is not interfered with.

Taking note of the same, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.1,89,312/- towards loss of future income due to disability, which is just and reasonable and same is not disturbed.
18.

Taking note of the injuries suffered by the claimant and evidence of CW1-doctor coupled with Ex.C2-Disability Certificate, we deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering as against Rs.25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has not granted any compensation on the head of loss of amenities.
Looking into the injuries sustained and the disability suffered by the claimant, we deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities.
The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.6,747/- towards medical expenses, as per - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7930-DB medical bills produced by the claimant, which is undisturbed.
The claimant was an inpatient for about 49 days in different hospitals.
Taking note of the same, it is jut and appropriate to award a sum of Rs.24,000/- towards loss of income during laid-up period for three months.

Thus, the claimant is entitled to modified compensation on the following heads:
Sl.No. Particulars Amount 1. Loss of earning capacity Rs.1,89,312/-
2. Pain and suffering Rs. 50,000/-
Gajanan @ Gajanand S/O Dharageppa ... vs Chandrashekhar S/O Malleshappa ... on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141131991/
6

3. Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
4.

Medical expenses Rs. 6,747/-
5. Food, Nourishment, attendant Rs. 25,000/-
 charges, conveyance etc.

6. Loss of income during laid-up Rs. 24,000/-
 period  Total Rs.3,45,059/-
19.
Thus, the claimant-Gajanan is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,45,059/- as against Rs.2,46,059/- awarded by the Tribunal.

20. In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) Both appeals are allowed in part.

b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the appellant/claimant in MFA No.103626/2019 - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7930-DB is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,45,059/- as against Rs.2,46,059/- awarded by the Tribunal and the claimant in MFA No.103625/2019 is entitled to total compensation of Rs.35,40,344/- as against Rs.23,99,944/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount in both the appeals shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petitions till realization.
d) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement in both the appeals shall be made as per award of the Tribunal.
e) Registry to transmit the TCR to the Tribunal forthwith.
f) Draw modified award accordingly.
